children: is getting into the lab-grown diamond business and opened a new manufacturing plant in Vietnam that will increase production by 50%.
“We are clearly building the capacity today for the growth of tomorrow that we expect,” Pandora CEO Berta de Pablos-Barbier said in an interview with CNBC.
The new facility in Ho Chi Minh City can reportedly produce as much as 60M pieces of jewelry per year, an increase of 50% in the company’s total manufacturing capacity.
The new facility and increased production expectations coincide with Pandora’s expansion into lab-grown diamonds, a rapidly growing new market and affordable alternative to mined diamonds.

“The consumer is making the choice [to lab-grown] based on a couple of criteria,” Pablos-Barbier said, citing sustainability and affordability as factors driving the explosive growth. According to industry data, the global lab-grown diamond market is currently valued at $30B to $34B and expected to nearly triple over the next 8 years.

title: Pandora's lab-grown diamonds; Vietnam facility to drive growth
